Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.state

Class SkullEyeState

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.state.SkullEyeState
public final class SkullEyeState extends Object
Eye state of a placed mob head and of a head item. A head carries the same EyeState.Snapshot a mob does, in a compound each loader's Mixin adds to the head block entity (SkullEyeState.Holder), saved under "somegoogly:data" in its data and replaced on every load. So the server's save, the clients' update packets, and a head item's BlockEntityTag all carry it: vanilla's placement loads it into the new block entity, and the head's loot copies it back onto the dropped item. Neither loader's own block-entity store serves here, since a plain load doesn't read either one back.

A head type borrows its mob's adult eye definition and shows only the eyes attached to the part of its mob that the head model reproduces (headParts(net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation, com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.HeadInfo)). Vanilla head types are matched by type, the Heads mod's by block id (entityFor(ResourceLocation)), so that mod is never referenced and its absence changes nothing. A head with no mob here (the dragon, other mods' heads, Heads' heads whose mob's eyes sit on a part the head doesn't reproduce) never has eyes.

Server mutations end in a block update, which resends the block entity's data to every client in range; clients only read the compound.

    • HEADS_MOBS

      public static final Map<String,net.minecraft.world.entity.EntityType<?>> HEADS_MOBS
      The Heads mod's heads by floor-block id path: the mob whose definition each borrows. Its wall blocks differ only by a _wall segment. Left out are the heads of mobs with no definition (axolotl, endermite, silverfish) and those whose mob's eyes sit on a part the head model doesn't reproduce (squid, glow squid, slime, magma cube).
